hook: 3,400 years ago, a clay tablet recorded a royal tragedy. Now 131 newly found tablets reveal what really happened in the Hittite court.

sections.voiceover: 3,400 years ago, a clay tablet recorded a royal tragedy.
sections.visual_cue: Ancient clay tablet with cuneiform script, stable composition on neutral background.
sections.animation_cue: Fade in from black, stable frame

sections.voiceover: Archaeologists at Kayalıpınar in central Turkey discovered 131 cuneiform tablets in the royal archive.
sections.visual_cue: Excavation trench with archaeologists carefully working, stable medium shot.

sections.voiceover: Combined with 53 pieces found in 2025 at Šamuḥa, that makes 184 total archive pieces.
sections.visual_cue: Clay fragments on padded museum shelves, stable overhead shot.

sections.voiceover: The tablets reveal a deadly epidemic during King Tudhaliya II's reign — including a nursing princess who died.
sections.visual_cue: Damaged clay edges with cuneiform markings under raking light, stable macro shot.

sections.voiceover: 131 cuneiform tablets revealed a lost royal tragedy.
sections.visual_cue: Excavated Kayalıpınar site at dusk, stable wide shot.
